body:
Parent: #1172

## Problem

The mobile and desktop clients currently present separate-looking session
catalogs. A chat created on mobile can run and respond without appearing in
the desktop client, while existing desktop sessions do not appear on mobile.
This makes it unclear whether both clients are operating on the same Mac,
project, user, and OpenCode engine.

This is a post-beta corrective issue and does not block the first
"somewhat functional" mobile release.

## Outcome

Desktop and mobile consume one authoritative, user/project-scoped session
catalog. Existing sessions and changes made on either client become visible on
the other without creating duplicate transcript or session records.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After pairing to the same Mac and selecting the same project/user, mobile
      and desktop list the same eligible existing sessions.
- [ ] A session created on mobile appears on desktop, and a session created on
      desktop appears on mobile, through realtime delivery or a bounded
      authoritative refresh.
- [ ] Rename, archive/restore, and delete state converge across both clients.
- [ ] Session identity remains stable across refresh/reconnect; no duplicate
      rows or transcript messages are introduced.
- [ ] Project and user ownership filtering remains server-side and fail-closed.
- [ ] Offline mobile cache is secret-free, clearly marked stale/read-only, and
      reconciles on reconnect.
- [ ] Automated coverage exercises two clients against the same gateway, and a
      physical-device smoke confirms cross-device visibility.

## Likely files

- `apps/mobile/providers/services/session-service.ts`
- `apps/mobile/providers/opencode-provider.tsx`
- `apps/mobile/providers/opencode-provider-selectors.ts`
- `apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/agents.tsx`
- `apps/mobile/app/agents/chats/[sessionId].tsx`
- `apps/desktop_flutter/lib/features/agents/`
- `apps/api_server/src/` mobile gateway/session routes and realtime events

## Required tests / evaluation

- Mobile service/provider contract covering initial history plus realtime
  create/update/delete reconciliation.
- Server contract proving user/project-scoped session listing.
- Desktop/mobile integration test against one gateway.
- Physical iPhone + desktop smoke: create one chat on each client and confirm
  both appear on both clients without duplicates.

## Safety / out of scope

- Do not broaden Device-token access or expose filesystem roots, provider
  credentials, or another user's sessions.
- Do not create a second session database or copy transcripts between stores.
- Does not block the first functional beta release.
title: iOS: synchronize session history and lifecycle across mobile and desktop
